subject: Cognitive Science
title: The McGurk Effect
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The McGurk Effect.

hook.text: Watch a video of someone saying 'ga' while the audio plays 'ba.' You'll hear 'da.' A sound that doesn't exist.

buildup.text: The McGurk effect shows that speech perception isn't just auditory—your brain fuses visual lip movements with sound.

discovery.text: Discovered accidentally in 1976, it proves that hearing and vision are combined before conscious awareness.

twist.text: Close your eyes and the illusion vanishes. Open them and it returns—even if you know the trick.

climax.text: This is why phone calls feel harder than video calls. Without lip-reading cues, your brain has less input to work with.

punchline.text: What you see changes what you hear.

quiz.question: What causes the McGurk effect?
options: The brain fuses visual and auditory speech cues
